citations.quote: The protocol planned for a single primary efficacy endpoint: the percent change from baseline in the “average pain for the past 24 hours” of NPRS score during Weeks 2-8.

Patients were adult males and females with neuropathic pain due to PHN. A total of 402 patients were randomized to the study, 206 to the Qutenza treatment group and 196 to the low dose control group. target_moa.text: Capsaicin is a highly selective agonist of the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) receptor; following exposure, cutaneous nociceptors become less sensitive (“defunctionalization”), reducing spontaneous and evoked painful sensations.

citations.quote: Capsaicin, the active pharmaceutical ingredient in the patch, is a highly selective agonist for the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 receptor (TRPV1).
Following exposure to capsaicin, cutaneous nociceptors can become less sensitive to a variety of stimuli, including further capsaicin exposure or thermal stimuli.

summary.text: NDA 022395 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) for QUTENZA (capsaicin) 8% patch and underwent Standard review. The product received orphan-drug designation for PHN, which exempted it from PREA pediatric requirements. No advisory committee meeting was held. It was approved first cycle for management of neuropathic pain associated with postherpetic neuralgia.
